column1: # The modules of the game code, and the one module every file under Assets/WarCore belongs to.
# M <tab> number <tab> key <tab> block <tab> name <tab> the question this module alone answers
# F <tab> module key <tab> a file, or a pattern (* stays inside one folder, ** crosses folders), relative to Assets/WarCore
# One file, one module. A file's own row beats a pattern; between patterns the longer one wins.
# A new file that no row names fails the check: give it a row here before it is merged.
# Tests/, Verification/ and Unity/Tests/ only check the game and belong to no module.

column6: What the ground, walls, floors and placed objects are, and how a map is read, written, built and edited
How big a unit is, which posture it holds and which way it faces
How a unit gets from here to there: paths, steps, slopes, dashes, passing others
Who can see whom, and which enemy is the nearest visible one
How weapons, melee, projectiles and blasts hit, and how accurate a shot is
How much life a unit has, what damage does to it, when it is down or dead, which actions its state allows
Actions with a cost and a cooldown, and the lasting effects they leave
What a computer-run unit, its squad and its commander decide to do
Who is friend, enemy or neutral to whom
How a match runs: capture, reinforcements, respawn, who wins
Using things in the world: triggers, doors, pickups, trade
How a player's input becomes a unit's action
Deterministic numbers, entities, scheduling, space queries, saving and state hashes
How a content pack and a map become a running match
Drawing what the rules computed, without deciding anything
